A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HILBERT system and benchmark study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding algorithms, prompts, proofs, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original HILBERT evaluations on MiniF2F and PutnamBench, retrieval and recursion-depth ablations, compute-scaling analyses, and generated-proof statistics.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds gpt-oss-120b evaluations, a separate PutnamBench rerun, compute summaries, and failure-stage measurements.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 makes limited procedural corrections to the pseudocode: Algorithm 2 concatenates sketch_assembled instead of sketch; Algorithm 4 updates the sketch before reverification; Algorithm 8 explicitly supplies the problem and missing identifiers to retrieval. The recursive architecture and Appendix A.2 prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 244 MiniF2F test problems and September 2025 PutnamBench collection of 660 problems. New reasoner configurations and inference budgets do not introduce different datasets, mathematical tasks, or input environments.

E2.justification: V2 adds BFS-Prover-V2-32B with Planner, reported at 95.1%, to the MiniF2F comparison in Table 1. Existing external comparators remain. The added HILBERT configurations using gpt-oss-120b are configurations of the proposed system.

E3.justification: V2 adds the gpt-oss-120b reasoner configuration and a separate PutnamBench evaluation using strictly one HILBERT attempt per problem with compute tracking. Tables 4–5 summarize compute over successful proofs. Existing benchmark splits and recursion depth remain unchanged; the multiple-retry description clarifies the retained headline experiment.

E4.justification: Appendices A.6–A.7 substantially expand the diagnostics with PutnamBench compute-scaling curves, resource-distribution summaries, and systematic classification of failures into sketch generation, sketch assembly, and shallow solving. The original depth and retrieval ablations remain. MiniF2F token-scaling plots are relocated, not newly introduced analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same baseline uncertainty values. V2 adds no seed information, repeated-run variability estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New cost means, medians, and failure proportions describe empirical outcomes; inference retries are search-budget settings rather than statistical replications.

E6.justification: The headline 99.2% MiniF2F and 462/660 PutnamBench results remain unchanged. V2 adds gpt-oss-120b results of 90.8% and 88/660, respectively, plus 55.9% for Gemini under the separate one-attempt PutnamBench protocol. Figure 7 and Tables 4–6 add substantial compute and failure findings. These are additional results, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or a new formal analysis. The mathematical statements and reasoning in the worked Lean proof in Appendix A.5 are retained; removed comments and reformatted code do not change the proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the PutnamBench claim from the best known result to the strongest known result from a publicly available model. The conclusion incorporates gpt-oss-120b and expands the reported MiniF2F range to 90.8–99.2%, while explicitly associating 70.0% PutnamBench performance with Gemini. Core contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of heavy-tailed compute consumption and model-dependent bottlenecks: gpt-oss-120b primarily struggles to construct usable sketches, whereas Gemini more often fails when proving subgoals. It suggests additional attempts could mitigate failures. Existing explanations concerning retrieval, reasoner strength, and long-proof generation are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and first discloses that the headline PutnamBench result used exhaustive computation with multiple retries and no compute tracking. It documents logging for the new analysis and corrects pseudocode data flow. The extensive prompts, software versions, and parallelization description were already present.

R1.justification: V2 adds the gpt-oss model card by Agarwal et al., Kontorovich's The Shape of Math to Come, and Xin et al.'s BFS-Prover-V2 work. Related work now includes BFS-Prover V2, but the central positioning relative to informal reasoning, specialized provers, and earlier decomposition frameworks remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized wording corrections, moving the token-scaling explanation into Section 4.2, inserting the failure-analysis subsection, removing explanatory comments from the worked proof, and updating correspondence and acknowledgments. This is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICLR typography, headers, margins, and reformatted code blocks throughout. It combines v1 Figures 3 and 6 into a four-panel Figure 3, renumbers the retained prover/verifier plots, adds the PutnamBench Figure 7 and Tables 4–6, and expands Tables 1–2. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through the separate one-attempt PutnamBench evaluation, open-reasoner results, failure diagnostics, code-access information, and pseudocode corrections. These additions help readers interpret the retained headline results. However, the compute budget behind the 70.0% result remains unaccounted for, and the new failure discussion contains a denominator error, reporting 68/660 as 11.91%. The revision offers a useful but limited net quality improvement.
